records.title: Email-verification link still lands behind the protected shell; self-serve signup cannot complete on any non-dev deployment
records.evidenceAtHead: client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:175-176 auth-route regex is still /^\/(concept2cure\/)?(login|signup|password-reset)(\/|\?|$)/. The only diff to this file since 92ccdba1 is the returnTo query at :88-95. Evaluated under node at HEAD: '/concept2cure/verify-email authRoute=false v2Owns(protected)=true'. The <Route path="/concept2cure/verify-email"> at :220 is dead code because the uiV2Owns branch at :181-188 returns <ProtectedZenApp/> first. server/services/email-verification.ts:26,64 still mails `${base}/concept2cure/verify-email#token=...`. server/routes/auth.ts:936 sets verificationRequired = !isDevAuthAllowed(), which is true unless NODE_ENV=development AND ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1 (server/auth/dev-auth-policy.ts:24-29). auth.ts:1144-1162: signup returns 201 with no session. auth.ts:512-526: login refuses with 403 AUTH_EMAIL_UNVERIFIED. Concept2CureLogin.tsx:479-482: the 'verify' button calls setLocation('/concept2cure/verify-email'), which loops back into the same redirect. Reproduced at HEAD with a scratch vitest file outside the repo, using the same mocks as v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx: <ZenRouter/> signed out at /concept2cure/verify-email#token=... printed PATH_AFTER=/concept2cure/login?returnTo=%2Fconcept2cure%2Fverify-email and VERIFY_PAGE_RENDERED=false. The token fragment is dropped. auth/__tests__/VerifyEmail.test.tsx mocks wouter and tests the component in isolation, so it cannot catch the routing defect. tests/e2e has no verify-email spec. The invite path is unaffected: server/services/password-setup-token.ts:50 builds /concept2cure/password-reset?token=, which matches the regex.
records.remaining: Whole finding. The mailed link /concept2cure/verify-email#token=... is routed to the protected shell, so it redirects to sign-in and drops the token. Every self-serve account stays pending_verification for good, and the login page's 'verify' button loops. No test proves the route is public.
records.severityRationale: Not P0 for this pilot. It is sales-led, and invitees activate through /concept2cure/password-reset?token=, which is inside the public-route regex, so the pilot can start. It is P1 because self-serve signup is always mounted in production (no flag on POST /api/auth/signup, auth.ts:887). A pilot user's colleague or a prospect who uses 'Create account' gets an org and a pending admin that can never activate, and lands in a sign-in loop. The fix is S.
records.humanTestingNote: Where it shows: any deployment with dev-auth off (NODE_ENV not 'development' or ALLOW_DEV_AUTH not '1') and SMTP configured. The tester signs up, gets the e-mail and clicks the link. They land on the sign-in page with returnTo=/concept2cure/verify-email and the account is not confirmed. Signing in then says the address is unverified, and the 'verify' button returns to sign-in. Without SMTP, signup instead answers 'Sign-up is not available right now.' Locally with NODE_ENV=development and ALLOW_DEV_AUTH=1, signup skips verification and the bug cannot be seen. Workaround: provision testers through Admin > invite member. The activation link /concept2cure/password-reset?token=... works.
records.instructions:
1. Work on concept2cure-v2 only (CLAUDE.md Rule 0). Pull with --ff-only or merge, never rebase.
2. Write the failing test first: client/src/concept2cure/router/__tests__/publicAuthRoutes.test.tsx (jsdom). Copy the mocks from client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx:17-28: useAuth unauthenticated, ../../auth with VerifyEmail rendering a test id, Concept2CureLogin, IdleSessionGuard and V2App. Call window.history.replaceState(null,'','/concept2cure/verify-email#token=<60+ char token>'), render <ZenRouter/>, wait, then assert that window.location.pathname stays '/concept2cure/verify-email' and the VerifyEmail test id is rendered. Run it at HEAD and confirm it FAILS: the path becomes /concept2cure/login?returnTo=%2Fconcept2cure%2Fverify-email. Keep that red output for the commit message.
3. Create shared/constants/public-auth-paths.ts. Export PUBLIC_AUTH_SEGMENTS = ['login','signup','password-reset','verify-email'] as const, VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH = '/concept2cure/verify-email', PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH = '/concept2cure/password-reset', and isPublicAuthPath(location) built from the segments: ^/(concept2cure/)?(seg1|seg2|...)(/|\?|$).
4. client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:175-176: replace the inline regex with isPublicAuthPath(location) imported from '@shared/constants/public-auth-paths'. Leave the existing <Route path="/concept2cure/verify-email"> at :220 as it is; it becomes reachable.
5. server/services/email-verification.ts:26: re-export VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH from shared/constants/public-auth-paths instead of declaring it. server/services/password-setup-token.ts:50: build the URL from PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH. After this, the client router and the mailed links read one list.
6. Add a parity case to the same test file: isPublicAuthPath(VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH) and isPublicAuthPath(PASSWORD_SETUP_PATH) are true, and so is '/concept2cure/login', the SSO handoff base in server/routes/sso.ts:111. Show that removing 'verify-email' from the list makes it fail.
7. Re-run the step-2 test and confirm it passes. Also run client/src/concept2cure/auth/__tests__/VerifyEmail.test.tsx and client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/deepLinkKeepsProgram.test.tsx and confirm both still pass.
8. Add an end-to-end proof: tests/e2e/signup-verify.e2e.spec.ts, run in a CI job with NODE_ENV=production-like (ALLOW_DEV_AUTH unset) and a Mailpit service container (SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS pointed at it). Steps: sign up through /concept2cure/signup, read the captured mail through the Mailpit HTTP API, open the link, see the confirmed state, sign in and land on /concept2cure. Negative case: a tampered token shows the not-confirmed message and offers a new link.
9. Commit with the red/green outputs and push to concept2cure-v2.
records.acceptance: (a) The new router test fails at HEAD (redirect to /concept2cure/login) and passes after the change. (b) The parity test fails if 'verify-email' is removed from PUBLIC_AUTH_SEGMENTS. (c) With dev-auth off and a mail sink, the Playwright spec signs up, opens the captured link, sees 'confirmed', signs in and lands on the shell; a tampered token shows the expired or invalid message. (d) The server's VERIFY_EMAIL_PATH and the client router import the same constant (grep shows one definition).
records.dependencies: A mail-capture service (e.g. Mailpit) in the e2e CI job, for step 8 only. Founder decision on whether self-serve signup is offered during the pilot: if not, also gate POST /api/auth/signup and the signup link behind an explicit setting (separate change).

records.title: Rail rebuilt as one list, but only five of the eight launch apps have an entry (no Authoring, Submission Readiness or CMC), and it still opens icon-only

RAIL_CORE is now New conversation (target home), Projects, Vault, Submission Center, Quality, Reporting & analytics, My work (tasks, filtered to the person's own) and Conversation. Shell.tsx:230 renders that single list with no section headers, so the empty 'Science & intelligence' header is gone. tasks appears once. The label is 'Projects'. Quality is on the rail and out of NAV_HIDDEN. Client categories moved to the account menu (Shell.tsx:370, clientType). The top-bar client-domain switcher was removed (25d79c99c). The logo opens Home (Shell.tsx:204-216). Still open: computed at HEAD by running tsx against shared/constants/launch-scope.ts LAUNCH_APPS (now eight apps: CMC and Reporting were added). On the rail: projects, vault, submission-center, qms and reporting are true; authoring, submission-readiness and cmc are false. Authoring's old entries (logo, 'Recent Documents') are both gone. Its editor list (document-authoring) is now reached only from in-surface links (e.g. Vault.tsx:1314), ⌘K or the Apps catalog. dispatch-readiness is reachable only from Project home > Markets 'Open readiness' (surfaces/ProjectMarkets.tsx:313-317), ⌘K or the Apps catalog. V2App.tsx:175 DEFAULT_PREFS.railCollapsed is still true, so the first run is icon-only. The account menu still offers every client type (CLIENT_CATEGORIES, registryModel.ts:346-355), including device categories for a biotech tenant. v2/__tests__/shellNav.test.tsx:130 pins the current list ('exactly the places, in order'); no test asserts that every LAUNCH_APPS entry has a rail entry.
records.fixedBy: 9a94754c6: registryModel.ts:141-150 RAIL_CORE and Shell.tsx:230, one list, no sections. 25d79c99c: top-bar client selector removed, client type only in the account menu. beea5f91e: Reporting & analytics added to the launch scope.
records.remaining: Authoring (document-authoring), Submission Readiness (dispatch-readiness) and CMC / Module 3 (cmc, where entitled) have no rail entry. The rail defaults to collapsed (icon-only). Every tenant gets the full client-type picker. The 'Quality' label differs from the catalog name 'QMS controlled documents'.
records.severityRationale: The defects that made the nav misleading are fixed: the empty section, the duplicate entry, wrong labels and locked entries. Five launch apps are one click away. Authoring and Submission Readiness are still reachable through Vault documents, Project home, ⌘K and the Apps catalog, and a founder-supported pilot can coach that. It still needs fixing before enterprise GA.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers told to open Authoring or Submission Readiness will find no rail entry. To reach Authoring, open a document from Vault or Project home, press ⌘K and type 'authoring', or use the account menu > Apps catalog. To reach Submission Readiness, open a project and use the Markets panel's 'Open readiness', or ⌘K 'readiness'. The rail opens as icons only on first run; the expand toggle is at its foot.
records.instructions:
1. Founder/CPO decision first, because docs/design/ONE_ANA_ONE_CANVAS.md §5 deliberately routes Authoring through documents. Confirm that every app in shared/constants/launch-scope.ts LAUNCH_APPS (:51-172) gets a rail entry. Record the decision in §5 and in the RAIL_CORE header comment at client/src/concept2cure/v2/registryModel.ts:100-140.
2. Write the failing test first: in client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/shellNav.test.tsx add 'every launch app has a rail entry'. For each app in LAUNCH_APPS, assert RAIL_CORE.some(r => app.surfaces.includes(r.target ?? r.id)). Run it at HEAD and confirm it fails for authoring, submission-readiness and cmc.
3. registryModel.ts:141-150: insert { id: 'document-authoring', label: 'Authoring', icon: 'penLine' } after vault, { id: 'dispatch-readiness', label: 'Submission Readiness', icon: 'checkSquare' } after submission-center, and { id: 'cmc', label: 'CMC / Module 3', icon: 'beaker' } after quality. records.acceptance: (a) The 'every launch app has a rail entry' test fails at HEAD on authoring, submission-readiness and cmc, and passes after. (b) A DOM test clicks each rail entry and lands on a surface in LAUNCH_SURFACE_IDS. (c) A first run with no stored prefs at 1280px shows the rail expanded with text labels. records.title: <html lang> still follows the browser or stored language on an English-only shell (WCAG 3.1.1); the 18-language switcher translates only the auth pages
records.evidenceAtHead: No commits to client/src/i18n since 92ccdba1. client/src/i18n/index.ts:35-40: applyDocumentLanguage writes document.documentElement.lang and dir from the active i18n language. :61 detection order is ['localStorage','navigator']. :67-68 applies it at init and on every change. client/index.html:2 lang="en" is overwritten at boot, because main.tsx:17 imports i18n before rendering. contexts/LanguageContext.tsx:140 then applies the account's preferences.language. Locale files per language (en, de and ja checked): auth 127, common 31, home 6, settings 4 keys. useTranslation is used only in Concept2CureLogin, VerifyEmail, SignupVerifyStep, ZenSignup, IdleSessionGuard and LanguageSwitcher itself; 0 of the 226 TSX files under client/src/concept2cure/v2. LanguageSwitcher is rendered only in Concept2CureLogin, VerifyEmail and ZenSignup. No test asserts the document language; CI has only check-i18n-integrity, which checks key parity.
records.remaining:
Whole finding:
- Every shell surface carries the browser's language tag over English content.
- The idle-timeout dialog inside the shell is translated while the shell is not.
- The switcher implies a localisation that covers only sign-in, sign-up and verify.
records.severityRationale: The pilot is one US, English-language biotech, so this does not stop the pilot or a core journey. It is a WCAG 3.1.1 failure that a VPAT or accessibility review will flag, and it affects screen-reader users with non-English OS locales, so it must be fixed before enterprise GA. The fix is S.
records.humanTestingNote: English-locale testers will not see it. A tester whose browser is German, French or Japanese sees sign-in, sign-up and the idle-timeout warning translated, and the rest of the app in English. A screen reader reads the English app with that language's voice. Workaround: set the browser to English, or choose English in the sign-in language switcher (stored in localStorage 'c2c.language').
records.instructions:
1. Get the founder's answer to open question 4 (launch languages). The steps below assume English-only at launch. If any other language is in scope, the alternative is to externalise the launch surfaces' strings (XL) instead.
2. Write the failing test first: client/src/i18n/__tests__/documentLanguage.test.ts (jsdom). Set localStorage 'c2c.language'='de' (or stub navigator.language='de-DE'), import '@/i18n', await i18n.changeLanguage('de'), and assert document.documentElement.lang === 'en'. Run it at HEAD and confirm it fails ('de').
3. client/src/i18n/index.ts:35-40 and :67-68: stop writing the i18n language to document.documentElement. Either delete applyDocumentLanguage and its two calls, leaving client/index.html:2 lang="en" authoritative, or make it always set 'en'/'ltr'.
4. Mark the translated subtrees instead (WCAG 3.1.2):
   - client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenAuthLayout.tsx: get i18n from useTranslation(), compute def = getLanguageDef(i18n.language) (client/src/i18n/languages.ts:60), and add lang={def.code} dir={def.dir} to the root element.
   - Do the same on the dialog root in client/src/concept2cure/components/session/IdleSessionGuard.tsx, whose strings are translated inside the English shell.
5. client/src/index.css:1020-1043: change the html-anchored rules (html:lang(ja) .greetH1 and the like) to :lang(ja) .greetH1, and delete the :lang(ja) body rules. CJK typography then applies inside the auth container's [lang] subtree.
6. client/src/components/i18n/LanguageSwitcher.tsx:1-12: correct the docblock, which claims the switcher is used in module TopBars and settings. Keep it on the auth pages only. Do not add it to the shell until shell strings are externalised. Nothing is deleted, so no replacement path is needed.
7. Extend the step-2 test: render ZenAuthLayout with the language set to 'de' and assert its root has lang="de" while documentElement.lang stays 'en'. Re-run and confirm green. Run node scripts/ci/check-i18n-integrity.mjs.
8. Optional: in the Playwright launch-surface run, add a context with locale 'de-DE' and assert document.documentElement.lang === 'en' on each launch surface (axe rule html-lang-valid). Commit on concept2cure-v2.
records.acceptance: (a) The new test fails at HEAD (lang 'de') and passes after. (b) With browser locale de-DE, ja-JP or fr-FR, document.documentElement.lang is 'en' on every shell surface. (c) The auth layout root and the idle dialog carry lang matching the chosen language. (d) check-i18n-integrity stays green.
records.dependencies: Founder answer on launch languages (question 4). If a non-English language is in scope, this becomes an XL externalisation of the launch surfaces.
